entries.hypothesis: The LP2 0-54 keystream was generated INSIDE the typesetting document: by a TeX-side PRNG (pgf's \pgfmathrandominteger, the lcg package's \rand, random.tex's \setrannum, or pdfTeX's \pdfuniformdeviate) invoked from the LaTeX source that produced the 6.00x9.00-inch runic PDF, reduced to Z_29 by one of the idiomatic package calls.
entries.prior_from: round18/L1-toolchain/RESULTS.md §6.2 rank 5, shift x2, 'never swept, never considered'. Facts F4 (400 dpi, 2400x3600 px = exactly 6.00x9.00 in), F5 (runes typeset from a proportional font, so character data before pixels), F10 (none of 11 stock Unicode runic faces; allrunes named as the live alternative), F2 (Ghostscript render => a PDF/PostScript source), F6/F7 (Ubuntu 11.04-12.04, GnuPG 1.4.11).
entries.threshold: V1 byte-exact equality against sequences emitted by the real TeX binaries, element for element; V2 >= 2 of 4 generators must pass; V3 pgf 2.10 == pgf 3.1.x; V4 both Lehmer multipliers primitive roots mod 2^31-1; V5/V5a ground-truth plant-and-recover.
entries.positive_control_detail: V5 AS PRE-REGISTERED: FAIL. It asked for the planted phase to rank #1 at rigid rune agreement 1.00; the key-skip filter makes that unattainable by construction, because the rigid optimum is the planted phase ADVANCED by the number of key skips. That mis-aimed gate is recorded, not edited, and the replacement is in a dated PREREG addendum. V5a: PASS - planted phase rank #2 of 80,004 inside the 1+n_skips band, rigid argmax at phase+2 with 2 skips, wrong-phase null mean 0.0342 / max 0.0917 (1/29 = 0.0345), and the skip-aware beam at the planted phase recovers 1.0000 of the known plaintext at score -4.2247 (recorded, not a decision statistic). The planted pad was taken from a real pdflatex run, not from Python, so a Python-side bug could not cancel itself out.

pgf.note: the multiplier is 69621, NOT the 16807 the source comment lists as an alternative

lcg.reduction: rejection then first + z mod R

random_tex.reduction: v = (z-1) div (2147483645 div R), rejected unless v < R

pdftex.note: init_randoms halves |seed| until < 2^28, which collapses the seed space to 2^28

result.era_correctness: pgf 2.00 (TeX Live 2009 = Ubuntu 11.04/11.10/12.04) and pgf 2.10 have a byte-identical \pgfmathgeneratepseudorandomnumber; reference vectors from vendored pgf 2.10 match installed pgf 3.1.11a on 76/76.
result.single_cycle_detail: 69621 and 16807 are both primitive roots mod 2^31-1 (verified against every prime factor of 2^31-2 = 2*3^2*7*11*31*151*331); each generator has ONE cycle of length 2147483646, so every seed and every offset is a phase of one master stream. B-04's offset ladder and B-02's key-index-0 assumption are ABSORBED for pgf/lcg/random.tex; they are NOT absorbed for pdfTeX, whose 55-word state gives disjoint trajectories.

entries.coverage: ZERO decodes of coverage. This is a Phase-1 generator lane: it delivers four byte-exact generators, a keystream interface, and an exact space statement, and it HOLDS at the scoring boundary because Round 19's Phase 0 (I1/I2/I3) had not been certified. A single labelled pilot of 10,000 decodes was run for plumbing and timing only, with `pilot: true, interpretable: false` in its SWEEPROW header; no score in it is interpreted and no candidate was escalated. Anyone citing this entry as coverage of the TeX family is citing it wrongly.
entries.not_covered: Everything. Specifically: (1) the whole 1.85e11-decode space; (2) the lcg package's DEFAULT seed, which depends on \inputlineno and \value{page} as well as the clock - samplable, not enumerable, and not sampled; (3) pdfTeX's DEFAULT seed, set from wall-clock microseconds - not enumerable at all; (4) per-page or per-line reseeding (an author calling \pgfmathsetseed once per page - the B-04 stage-C shape); (5) any constant c not in {0,1} added to the reduced key, i.e. a general Caesar; (6) \pgfmathrandomitem over a declared rune list, which is covered as a STREAM but whose list ordering would impose an unknown alphabet permutation; (7) LuaTeX math.random, which is glibc rand() and therefore G1's space, handed off with its Lua 5.1 scaling rather than re-swept; (8) XeTeX, which had no \uniformdeviate in the TeX Live 2009 era.
entries.reopens_if: Phase 2 (S1) runs it. The gate is K2: a planted phase must survive a 1e-3 rigid prefilter cut in >= 50% of 200 trials. If it does, complete enumeration of the three Lehmer families is ~18 h of wall clock on this box (13 h of numpy prefilter + a beam stage sized by the cut, ~4.4 h at a 1e-6 band-max cut). If it does not, G4 restricts to Tier 1: pgf's 8,627 distinct default seeds (69,016 decodes, 2.0 h at the drift preset on 6 cores), random.tex's 3,214,080 date-init seeds, and 0..2^20 author-typed integers.
entries.notes: Nothing in liber-primus/LEDGER.json's 62 prior entries has a TeX-internal RNG as its hypothesis, in any status/coverage/not_covered field - confirmed by keyword scan for tex|latex|pgf|lcg|typeset|allrunes, which matched 15 entries in prose only. The most consequential number this lane measured is not a generator constant: I1's repaired `drift` preset costs 226x the repo's `exact` preset beam-only and 36.5x end-to-end, so on 6 cores the repaired instrument runs at ~9.7 decodes/s = ~5.9e6 decodes/week. Phase 2's budget is therefore a decision about WHICH ~1e6-1e7 decodes, not a coverage figure - and the Round-13-era 1,400 decodes/s figure no longer applies because it was measured without an adjudicator and with the unrepaired decoder.

entries.hypothesis: round18/L1 NC-5: 'the allrunes Type-1 faces are custom-encoded (not Unicode-mapped), so matching them requires an unordered glyph-slot search rather than a codepoint lookup.'
entries.threshold: Order-destroying permutation control: 200 refits against shuffled observed width vectors; the real assignment must beat the null at p <= 0.05 or the screen is declared uninformative.

result.nc5_verdict: FOUND-ERROR. NC-5's stated blocker is false for the files L1 already holds: the 218 allrunes .pfb charstrings carry ordinary Adobe glyph names that ARE the transliteration letters (f u eth o r c g w h n i j p x s t b e m l eng oe d a ae y), so 26 of the 29 futhorc runes are a direct name lookup. Only EO / EA / IA lack an unambiguous name.

entries.coverage: A SCREEN, not a verdict. It shows LP2's per-rune ink-width assignment matches the allrunes Anglo-Frisian family far better than a shuffle. It does NOT discriminate allrunes from any other CORRECT futhorc face - every correct face has a narrow I and a wide X, so the permutation control separates 'a real futhorc' from 'a shuffle', nothing more. The fitted scale factors (0.40-0.84) are an artefact of normalising by each face's median glyph height and are NOT evidence of a condensed face.
entries.not_covered: L1's own font_match.py distance under its PC3a/PC3b controls, with these 72 allrunes faces in the bank. That is the measurement that could name the face, and it is now a codepoint lookup rather than a slot search.
entries.reopens_if: L1's matcher is re-run with the allrunes bank included. If a specific allrunes shape variant separates from the field, it pins the LaTeX source and with it the plausible package set - which is exactly the prior G4-TEX-RNG runs on.
